plain_english: Now the seventh chapter: the blessed Lord said, O Pārtha, with mind fixed in me, practicing yoga while taking refuge in me, you will know me wholly without doubt; hear that.
sanskrit_cite: atha saptamo'dhyāyaḥ   śrībhagavānuvāca   mayyāsaktamanāḥ pārtha | yogaṃ yuñjanmadāśritaḥ | asaṃśayaṃ  samagraṃ māṃ yathā jñāsyasi tacchṛṇu

plain_english: I will speak to you this knowledge with direct knowledge completely; having known it, nothing remains to be known, since in knowledge and action nothing of the knowable remains, because of fixity in knowledge and action.
sanskrit_cite: jñānaṃ te'haṃ savijñānamidaṃ vakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ | yajjñātvā na pūnaḥ kiṃcijjñātavyamavaśiṣyate | jñānavijñāne jñānakriye eva | tato na kiṃcidavaśiṣyate-sarvasva  jñeyasya jñānakriyāniṣṭhatvāt

plain_english: Among thousands of men someone strives for perfection; among strivers and accomplished ones someone knows me in truth. By this, all are not fit for this thing, because of its rarity; effort-worthy knowledge is declared.
sanskrit_cite: manuṣyāṇāṃ sahasreṣu kaścidyatati siddhaye | yatatāmapi  siddhānāṃ kaścinmāṃ vetti tattvataḥ | asya ca vastunaḥ sarvo na yogyaḥ | ityanena durlabhatvāt  yatnasevyatā-māha

plain_english: Earth, water, fire, wind, space, mind, intellect indeed, and ego: thus this divided nature of mine is eightfold.
sanskrit_cite: bhūmirāpo'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano buddhireva ca | ahaṅkāra itīyaṃ  me bhinnā prakṛtiraṣṭadhā

plain_english: Know my other superior nature, O mighty-armed, the living being by which this world is sustained; that which is seen by all people in the worldly state is one only, yet divided into eight modes; thus nonduality is shown even in nature-discussion, and she, having obtained livingness and personhood, is my superior nature, not another's, with both forms, varied manifold arrangement of knowable and knower, and from that indeed nature is the ground of all being, own-nature essence, always unfailing; this world-earth etc.
sanskrit_cite: apareyamitastvanyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām | jīvabhūtāṃ  mahābāho yayedaṃ dhāryate jagat | iyamiti-pratyakṣeṇa yā saṃsārāvasthāyāṃ  sarvajanaparidṛśyamānā | sā caikaiva satī prakārāṣṭakena  bhidyate iti ekaprakṛtyārabdhatvādekameva viśvamiti  prakṛtivāde'pyadvaitaṃ pradarśitam | saiva jīvatvaṃ-puruṣatvaṃ  prāptā parā mamaiva nānyasya ca | sobhayarūpā  vedyavedakātmakaprapañcoparacanavicitrā | tata eva  svātmavimalamukuratalakalitasakalabhāvabhūmiḥ svasvabhāvātmikā  satatamavyabhicāriṇī prakṛtiḥ | idaṃ jagat-bhūmyādi

plain_english: Ascertain that all beings have this as womb; I am the source and likewise dissolution of the whole world; do thus, and you indeed ascertain that I, become Vāsudeva, am source and dissolution of all; by this, the Lord is not different from nature, person, and supreme person, situated in every way by all-pervadingness; thus no difference-doctrine between Sāṃkhya and yoga is shown.
sanskrit_cite: etadyonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇītyupadhāraya | ahaṃ kṛtsnasya  jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayastathā | upadhāraya-abhyāsāhitānubhavakrameṇātmasamīpe kuru | evaṃ ca  tvamevopadhāraya-yadahaṃ vāsudevībhūtaḥ sarvasya prabhavaḥ  pralayaśca | aham-ityanena  prakṛtipuruṣapuruṣottamebhyo'vyatirikto'pīśvaraḥ sarvathā  sarvānugatatvena sthita iti sāṃkhyayogayornāsti bhedavādaḥ-iti  pradarśitam

plain_english: Nothing is higher than me; all this is strung in me like gems on a thread; though formless, I stand within all.
sanskrit_cite: mattaḥ parataraṃ nānyatkiñcidastu dhanañjaya | mayi sarvamidaṃ  protaṃ sūtre maṇigaṇā iva | sūtre maṇigaṇā eva-yathā  tanturanavadhriyamāṇarūpo'pyantarlīnatayā sthitaḥ evamahaṃ  sarvatra

plain_english: I am taste in waters, light in moon and sun, om in all Vedas, sound in space, and vigor in men.
sanskrit_cite: raso'hamapsu kaunteya prakāśaḥ śaśisūryayoḥ | praṇavaḥ  sarvavedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣaṃ nṛṣu | apsviti-sarvatrāsvādyamāno yo'nudbhinnamadhurādivibhāgaḥ  sāmānyaḥ so'ham | evaṃ prakāśaḥ-mṛdutvacaṇḍatvādirahitaḥ | khe-ākāśe yaḥ śabda iti sarvasyaiva śabdasya  nabhoguṇatvādatrāvadhāraṇam yaḥ kevalaṃ gaganaguṇatayā dhvaniḥ  saṃyogavibhāgādisāmagryantararahito'vahitahṛdayairbrahmaguhāgahan  agāmī yogigaṇaiḥ saṃvedyo'nāhatākhyaḥ  sakalaśrutigrāmānugāmī tadbhagavatastattvam | pauruṣaṃ-yena  tejasā puruṣo'hamiti sārvabhaumaṃ pratipadyate

plain_english: I am pure smell in earth, radiance in fire, life in all beings, and austerity in ascetics.
sanskrit_cite: puṇyaḥ pṛthivyāṃ gandho'smi tejaścā'smi vibhāvasau | jīvanaṃ  sarvabhūteṣu tapaścā'smi tapasviṣu | yo dharāyāṃ kevaladharmatayā gandhaguṇaḥ sa svabhāvapuṇyaḥ  pūtyutkaṭādīni tu bhūtāntarasaṃbandhāt | uktaṃ ca   dṛḍhaṃ bhūmiguṇādhikyāddurgandhyagniguṇodayāt | jaḍamambaguṇaudāryāt * * * * * * * * * * | ityādi

plain_english: Know me as the eternal seed of all beings; I am intelligence of the intelligent and radiance of the radiant.
sanskrit_cite: bījaṃ māṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ viddhi pārtha sanātanam | buddhirbuddhimatāmasmi tejastejasvināmaham

plain_english: I am strength free from desire and attachment, and desire not opposed to duty in beings.
sanskrit_cite: balaṃ balavatāmasmi kāmarāgavivarjitam | dharmāviruddho bhūteṣu  kāmo'smi bharatarṣabha | bījaṃ-sūkṣmamādikāraṇam | kāmarāgavivarjitaṃ  balaṃ-sakalavastudhāraṇasamartharmjorūpam | kāmaḥ-icchā  saṃvinmātrarūpā yasyā ghaṭapaṭādibhidharmarūpairnāsti  virodhaḥ | icchā hi sarvatra bhagavacchaktitayānuyāyinī na  kvacidvirudhyate dharmaistu-āgantukairghaṭapaṭādibhirbhidyate iti  tadupāsakatayā śuddhasaṃvitsvabhāvatvaṃ jñāninaḥ | uktaṃ ca  śivopaniṣadi-   icchāyāmathavā jñāne jāte cittaṃ niveśayet | (vi0 bhai0, 18)   iti | jāta eva natu bāhyaprasṛte ityarthaḥ | evaṃ vyākhyānaṃ  tyaktvā ye parasparānupaghātakaṃ trivargaṃ seveta-ityāśayena  vyācakṣate te saṃpradāyakramamajānānā bhagavadrahasyaṃ ca  vyācakṣāṇā namaskāryā eva

plain_english: Sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic states are from me; know them, but I am not in them; they are in me.
sanskrit_cite: ye caiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasāstāmasāśca ye | matta eveti tān  viddhi natvahaṃ teṣu te mayi

plain_english: The world is deluded by strand-born states and does not know the supreme imperishable Lord; knowing alone reaches the Lord-principle.
sanskrit_cite: tribhirguṇamayairbhāvairebhiḥ sarvamidaṃ jagat | mohitaṃ  nābhijānāti māmebhyaḥ paramavyayam | sattvādīni manmayāni natvahaṃ tanmayaḥ | ata eva ca bhagavanmayaḥ  sarvaṃ bhagavadbhāvena saṃvedayate | natu  nānāvidhapadārthavijñānaniṣṭho bhagavattatvaṃ pratipadyate iti  sakalamānasāvarjaka eṣa kramaḥ | anenaiva cāśayena vakṣyate  vāsudevaḥ sarvamiti iti jñānena yo  bahujanmopabhogajanitakarmasamatāsamanantarasamutpannaparaśaktipātān  u-gṛhītāntaḥ karaṇo'sau pratipadyate bhagavattatvaṃ sarvaṃ  vāsudevaḥ-iti buddhā sa mahātmā sa ca durlabha iti | evaṃ  hyabuddhyamānaṃ pratyuta sattvādibhirguṇairmohitamidaṃ jagat  guṇātītaṃ vāsudevatattvaṃ naivopalabhate | kathaṃ khalu sattvādimātrasthitā bhagavatastattvaṃ na viduḥ ?

plain_english: Divine maya is hard to cross, yet those who resort to the Lord cross it; knowing supreme Brahman sees the world undivided.
sanskrit_cite: ityāha   daivī hyeṣā guṇamayī mama māyā duratyayā | māmeva ye  prapadyante māyāmatitaranti te | devaḥ-krīḍākaraḥ tatra bhavā daivī-krīḍā mameyamityarthaḥ | tena sattvādīnāṃ vastutaḥ  saṃvinmātraparabrahmānatiriktatāyāmapi yattadatiriktatāvagamanaṃ  tadeva guṇatvaṃ-bhoktṛtattvapāratantryaṃ bhogyatvam | tacca  bhedātmakaṃ rūpaṃ saṃsāribhiranirvācyatayā tān prati  māyārūpam | ato ye paramārthabrahmaprakāśavidaste tadanatiriktaṃ  viśvaṃ paśyanto guṇānāṃ-sattvādīnāṃ guṇatālakṣaṇāṃ  bhedāvabhāsasvabhāvāṃ māyāmatitarantīti  māmeva-ityevakārasyāśayaḥ | ye tu yathāsthitaṃ  bhedāvabhāsamātraṃ viduste māyāṃ nātikrāmanti | tadyuktamuktaṃ  natvahaṃ teṣu-iti

plain_english: Evil-doers, deluded and lowest, do not resort to the Lord because maya steals their knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: na māṃ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ | māyayāpahṛtajñānā āsuraṃ bhāvamāśritāḥ | ye ca māṃ satyapyadhikāriṇi kāye nādriyante te duṣkṛtino  narādhamāḥ mūḍhāḥ-āsurāstāmasāḥ | iti māyāmahimaivāyam

plain_english: Four kinds of well-doers worship the Lord: the distressed, the seeker, the wealth-seeker, and the knower.
sanskrit_cite: caturvidhā bhajante māṃ janāḥ sukṛtinaḥ sadā | ārto  jijñāsurarthārthī jñānī ca bharatarṣabha

plain_english: Among them the knower, ever united, excels in single devotion; the knower is exceedingly dear to the Lord.
sanskrit_cite: teṣāṃ jñānī nityayukta ekabhaktirviśiṣyate | priyo hi  jñānino'tyarthamahaṃ sa ca mama priyaḥ

plain_english: All these devotees are noble, yet the knower is esteemed as the Lord's own self, established in the supreme goal.
sanskrit_cite: udārāḥ sarva evaite jñānī tvātmaiva me mataḥ | āsthitaḥ sa hi  yuktātmā māmevānuttamāṃ gatim

plain_english: After many births the knower resorts to the Lord as all; such a great soul is rare, while other devotees are noble yet seek limited ends, and the knower alone rests in nondifference.
sanskrit_cite: bahūnāṃ janmanāmante jñānavān māṃ prapadyate | vāsudevaḥ  sarvamiti sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ | ye tu māṃ bhajante te sukṛtinaḥ te ca catvāraḥ | sarve caite  udārāḥ yato'nye kṛpaṇabuddhayaḥ ārtinivāraṇamarthādi ca  tulyapāṇipādodaraśarīrasattvebhyo'dhikataraṃ vā ātmanyūnebhyo  mārgayante | jñānyapekṣayā tu nyūnasattvāḥ | yatasteṣāṃ  tāvatyapi bhedo'sti bhagavata idamahamabhilaṣyāmi-iti bhedasya  sphuṭapratibhāsāt | jñānī tu māmevābhedatayāvalambate iti  tato'hamabhinna eva | tasya cāhameva priyo natu phalam | ata eva sa  vāsudeva eva sarvam-ityevaṃ dṛḍhapratipattipavitrīkṛtahṛdayaḥ

plain_english: Those whose knowledge is stolen by desires resort to other deities, following rules determined by their own nature.
sanskrit_cite: kāmaistaistairhṛtajñānāḥ prapadyante'nyadevatāḥ | taṃ taṃ  niyamamāsthāya prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā

plain_english: Whoever wishes to worship a form with faith, the Lord grants that very unwavering faith.
sanskrit_cite: yo yo yāṃ yāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhayārcitumicchati | tasya  tasyācalāṃ śraddhāṃ tāmeva vidadhāmyaham

plain_english: Endowed with that faith, he seeks worship of that form and obtains desires ordained by the Lord for his benefit.
sanskrit_cite: sa tayā śraddhayā yuktastasyārādhanamīhate | labhate ca tataḥ  kāmān mayaiva vihitānhitān

plain_english: The fruit of those worshippers is perishable, while my devotees go to me; limited desire-bound worship yields limited fruit.
sanskrit_cite: antavattu phalaṃ teṣāṃ tadbhavatyalpamedhasām | devāndevayajo  yānti madbhaktā yānti māmapi | ye punaḥ svena svenottamādikāmanāsvabhāvena vicitreṇa  paricchinnamanasaste kāmanāpahṛtacetanāstatsamucitāmeva  mamaivāvāntaratanuṃ devatāviśeṣamupāsate | ato matta eva  kāmaphalamupādadate | kintu tasya anto'sti-nijayaiva vāsanayā  parimitīkṛtatvāt | ata evendrādibhāvanātātparyeṇa yāmādi  kurvantastathāvidhameva phalamupādadate | matprāptiparāstu māmeva | nanu sarvagate bhagavattattve kimiti devatāntaropāsakānāṃ mitaṃ  phalam ? ucyate-

plain_english: The foolish think the unmanifest has become manifest and do not recognize the Lord's supreme imperishable form; they know only a form suited to their own desire.
sanskrit_cite: avyaktaṃ vyaktimāpannaṃ manyante māmabuddhayaḥ | paraṃ  bhāvamajānanto mamāvyayamanuttamam | te khalu alpabuddhitvāt matsvarūpaṃ  pāramārthikamavidyamānavyaktikaṃ na pratyabhijānate | apitu  nijakāmanāsamucitākāraviśiṣṭajñānasvabhāvaṃ  vyaktimevāpannaṃ vidanti nānyathā | ata eva na nāmni ākāre vā  kaścidgrahaḥ | kintu siddhānto'yamatra yaḥ kāmanāparihāreṇa  yatkiṃciddevatārūpamālambate tasya tat śuddhamuktabhāvena  paryavasyati | viparyāttu viparyayaḥ

plain_english: I am not manifest to all, being covered by yoga-maya; this foolish world does not know me, the unborn and imperishable.
sanskrit_cite: nāhaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yogamāyāsamāvṛtaḥ | mūḍho'yaṃ  nābhijānāti loko māmajamavyayam

plain_english: I know past, present, and future beings, Arjuna, but no one knows me; I do not come within the range of all. The doubt begins: do actions at dissolution grant liberation, otherwise why does great dissolution arise?
sanskrit_cite: vedā'haṃ samatītāni vartamānāni cārjuna | bhaviṣyanti ca  bhūtāni māṃ tu veda na kaścana | sarveṣāṃ nāhaṃ gocaratāṃ prāpnomi | nanu ca karmāṇyeva kriyamāṇāni pralayakāle mokṣaṃ vidadhate | anyathā kimiti mahāpralaya upajāyate ? ityāśaṅkāyāmārabhate-

plain_english: Born of desire and hatred, all beings enter pair-delusion at creation, O Bharata; that delusion expands, and the whole world, capable only of its own action-organs, takes on a sleep-like state, not ended merely by that much experience.
sanskrit_cite: icchādveṣasamutthena dvandvamohena bhārata | sarvabhūtāni sammohaṃ  sarge yānti parantapa | icchādveṣakrodhamohādibhistāvanmohātmaka eva sa paraṃ  sphītībhāva-mupanīyate | yena prakṛtijaṭharāntarvarti samagrameva  jagat nijakāryakaraṇamātrākṣamameva prasuptatāmavalambate | āmohaṃ-vāsanānubhavātpratidinam rātrisamaye sauṣuptavat | natu  tāvatā vimuktarūpatā-mohānubhavasamāptau  punarvicitravyāpārasaṃsāradarśanāt

plain_english: Those people whose sin has come to an end, doers of meritorious action, freed from pair-delusion, worship me with firm vows.
sanskrit_cite: yeṣāṃ tvantaṃ gataṃ pāpaṃ janānāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām | te  dvandvamohanirmuktā bhajante māṃ dṛḍhavratāḥ

plain_english: Those who strive, resorting to me, for liberation from old age and death know that brahman, all inner action, and everything; but those whose darkness is destroyed know brahman as all, studded with the Lord's rays, a stream of darkness of old age and death.
sanskrit_cite: jarāmaraṇamokṣāya māmāśritya yatanti ye | te brahma tadviduḥ  kṛtsnamadhyātmaṃ karma cākhilam | ye tu vinaṣṭatāmasāḥ puṇyāpuṇyaparikṣayakṣemīkṛtātmānaste  vipāṭitamahāmohavitānāḥ sarvameva bhagavadraśmikhacitaṃ  jarāmaraṇamayatamisrasrutaṃ brahma vidanti

plain_english: Those who know me with adhibhuta and adhidaiva, and with adhiyajna, know me even at departure with united mind; they know my other forms as inner, elemental, divine, and sacrificial. Because their inner organ is always filled with the Lord, they know me; from which, those whose Lord-principle is known even before birth would remember the supreme Lord at the end. What of birth-service? Those who think so, silence itself is auspicious. Thus auspicious.
sanskrit_cite: sādhibhūtādhidaivaṃ māṃ sādhiyajñaṃ ca ye viduḥ | prayāṇakāle'pi ca māṃ te viduryuktacetasaḥ | ādhyātmikādhibhautikādhidaivikādhiyajñikāni ca mamaiva  rūpāntarāṇi | prayāṇakāle ca nityaṃ bhagavadbhāvitāntaḥ  karaṇatvānmāṃ jānanti yeto yeṣāṃ janmapūrvameva  bhagavattattvaṃ te'ntakāle parameśvaraṃ saṃsmareyuḥ | kiṃ  janmāsevanayā-iti ye manyante teṣāṃ tūṣṇīṃbhāva eva śobhana  iti śivam

plain_english: Here is the summary verse: clearly, the Lord's devotion-devoid wish-fulfilling cluster, suitable to the practitioner's wish, may fulfill desires; thus, in the Gita meaning-gathering composed by Abhinavagupta, the seventh chapter, seven.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   sphuṭaṃ bhagavato bhaktirāhitā kalpamañjarī | sādhakecchāsamucitāṃ yenāśāṃ paripūrayet | iti śrīmahāmaheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe saptamo'dhyāyaḥ
